close_reason: Landed paired with .62. The trait's signature now returns Option<AuthHeader<'_>>, and the trait rustdoc explicitly documents the static/single-header/per-connection limitation with the AWS SigV4 / OAuth-refresh workaround (custom TransportConfig with per-request middleware). The shape of the return type itself encodes the limitation, so the 'document the trait' recommendation in .20 is satisfied not by adding paragraphs to a Option<(&str, &str)>-shaped trait but by replacing the shape with one that conveys the limitation in the type system.
description:
auth.rs:138 — fn auth_header(&self) -> Option<(&str, &str)>

The trait signature commits the library to:

1. **Exactly one header.** A caller that needs a custom AuthProvider injecting BOTH Authorization and a vendor-specific header (e.g., X-Tenant-Id, X-Account-Hint, AWS SigV4's X-Amz-Date + Authorization pair) cannot do so. AWS SigV4 specifically requires 3+ headers per request including X-Amz-Date and X-Amz-Security-Token. Any real-world SigV4-style auth scheme is unimplementable against this trait. The current signature should have been Option<&[(&str, &str)]> or an iterator from day one.

2. **String-only values.** A custom AuthProvider that needs to compute a per-request HMAC signature (AWS SigV4, OAuth-style request signing where the signature depends on the request body) cannot do it: auth_header(&self) takes only &self, not the request. The trait should have taken &reqwest::Request or at least the URL/method/body. As shipped, only constant-credential schemes (Bearer, Basic, mTLS via TransportConfig) can be expressed.

3. **No async.** A custom AuthProvider that needs to refresh an expired OAuth token cannot do so without blocking-IO inside auth_header (and even then, sync IO inside a sync trait method called from an async path is a footgun). A future fix requires either async-trait or splitting into a separate refresh() method, both breaking changes.

The maintainer note (auth.rs:34, auth.rs:105) flags that 3 blanket impls must stay in sync — that's the cost of the current shape. The deeper issue is that the shape is wrong for the real-world auth schemes downstream consumers will hit (OAuth refresh, SigV4, request signing).

Workaround for callers today: implement the auth as a custom TransportConfig that injects per-request headers via reqwest middleware. That's an awkward layering inversion — TransportConfig should be about TLS, AuthProvider should be about auth — and it doesn't compose because TransportConfig builds the client once, not per-request.

Recommendation: before the next minor release, document explicitly in the trait docstring that this trait is intentionally limited to "static, per-connection single-header auth schemes" so callers know to use TransportConfig for anything more sophisticated. A future major bump can address the shape.
title: AuthProvider::auth_header signature locks header into single static pair
